concept.title: Language detection and fallback
concept.shortdesc: Choose Browser to have BPM resolve the first browser-preference language to one of six supported locales; an unsupported first language displays the interface in English.

section.title: Supported locales
section.p: BPM supports en, ru, de, zh-CN, fr, and es-ES as first-class interface locales.

section.title: Browser-language sources and matching
section.p: When you select Browser, BPM takes the first non-empty tag from navigator.languages, in the browser's preference order. Only when that list provides no tag does BPM use navigator.language. It changes underscores to hyphens and compares tags without case sensitivity. The matching rules accept en and en-*, ru and ru-*, de and de-*, zh-CN, zh-Hans, zh-Hans-*, and zh, fr and fr-*, and es-ES, es, and es-*. A tag that matches none of those rules resolves to en.

section.title: Fallback and stored choice
section.p: BPM currently ships a catalog for every supported locale. If a resolved target catalog is unavailable, BPM follows that locale's declared fallback, then English, and finally the first enabled catalog. Every non-English locale falls back to English. Therefore, with the shipped six-catalog set, an unsupported first browser language displays English. An explicit language selection is stored as bpm-lang-mode; Browser stores the browser-following mode rather than a frozen resolved locale, so BPM evaluates it again when it loads.

section.title: Content parity
section.p: Product documentation and screenshots must remain content-equivalent across all six locales, even when UI labels differ by language.
